properties.name: A decomposition is checkable against what the parent held, because delivery rolls up whether or not the children cover it
properties.statement: reflow2 rolls delivery UP a decomposition and never checks that the children COVER the parent. report.rs:566 is explicit: if a requirement has decomposed children, it is delivered if and only if every child is delivered — "let children = self.decomposed_children(requirement_id)?; if children.is_empty() { return Ok(false); } for child in &children { if !self.requirement_is_delivered_within(child, depth - 1)? { return Ok(false); } } Ok(true)". Nothing anywhere asks whether the children, taken together, amount to the parent. So a parent split into two children that address a tenth of it reports DELIVERED the moment both close, in the coverage number this project treats as ground truth (req:completion-computed: delivery is computed from the golden thread, never asserted). THE CONCRETE INSTANCE, and it is not hypothetical. This was first noticed on 2026-07-28 as a modelling risk, when DECOMPOSES was rejected as the edge type for two new requirements precisely because decomposing req:defaults-do-not-assert (ten measured instances) into two children would have reported it delivered with eight outstanding. Reviewing 01-systems_engineering.json the same day turned that risk into a field observation: reflow's own monolithic workflow was decomposed into 01a through 01f, and TWO CROSS-CUTTING TOP-LEVEL BLOCKS DID NOT SURVIVE. context_management (operations counter, degradation signals, refresh sequence, pre-operation checklist) and self_improvement (retrospective questions, metrics, improvement backlog) are present in all six monolithic workflows — 00-setup, 01-systems_engineering, 02-artifacts_visualization, 03-development, 04-testing_operations, feature_update — and absent from every one of 00a, 01a, 01b, 01c, 01d, 01e and 01f. Cross-referenced against workflow_master's phase assignments, context_management survives in roughly two of about sixteen live workflows. The discipline lived in every original file and largely did not make it into the decomposition, and nothing noticed for months. THE MECHANISM OF THE LOSS IS THE GENERAL CASE: a decomposition by SUBJECT drops what belongs to no single subject. Cross-cutting content has no natural child to land in, so it lands in none. That is exactly the failure a coverage check would catch and a roll-up will never notice, because the roll-up only ever asks whether each child is done. WHAT IS NOT BEING ASKED FOR: automatic refusal, or an LLM judging sufficiency. The honest form is a question put to the user at decomposition time — "does this set of children cover the parent, and what did the parent hold that none of them do?" — with the answer recorded, so a later reader can tell a deliberate narrowing from an accident. That fits the pattern the project already uses for gaps: report and ask, per dec:report-dont-judge, never decide. Note also the interaction with req:requirement-lineage, which distinguishes decomposed from derived: a DERIVED requirement adds new technical necessity and is not expected to cover anything, so any check must apply to decomposition alone. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing 01-systems_engineering.json. Anthony's word: capture it.
